 Order
This is the first application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) filed by the applicant for grant of bail.

2. The applicant has been arrested on 18.11.2025 in connection with Crime No. 11/2022 registered at Police Station Sehari District Ashoknagar, for offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 463,
464, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of IPC.

3. According to the prosecution case, the complainant, Rajdhar Singh, submitted a complaint petition before the learned Magistrate against the applicant and other co-accused persons, upon which the Magistrate directed the Station House Officer to register a First Information Report and conduct an investigation in respect of the alleged fraudulent loan allotment scam relating to land bearing Survey No. 1/9, area 5.289 hectares, situated at village Panchampur, against Arjun Singh and the co-accused namely NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31413 2 MCRC-55562-2025 Dhirendra Singh, Saurabh Tripathi, Pradeep Chaube, Dharmabai, Kartar Singh,
Ajab Singh, and Ashish Jain, and further granted liberty to take appropriate action and conduct investigation against any other person who may have aided the commission of the offence and to array such person as an accused in the case; in compliance with the said order, the police registered Arjun Singh Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7974372/
1 Crime No. 11/2022 under Sections 419, 420, 463, 464, 467, 468, 471, and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, and allegations were levelled against the applicant that, in conspiracy with the other co-accused persons, he had falsely impersonated the complainant.
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present matter and is innocent.

It is contended that the applicant was employed as an employee in HDFC Bank and neither committed any fraudulent act in relation to loans nor misrepresented anyone in connection with any alleged fake loan.
It is further submitted that senior officials of the bank have falsely implicated the applicant in this offence.

It is pertinent to note that the coordinate Bench has already granted the benefit of anticipatory bail to the co-accused, Smt. Dharma Bai, who identified the complainant Rajdhar, vide order dated 23.02.2022 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 8568 of 2022.

Learned counsel further submits that the conclusion of the trial is likely to take considerable time and there is no likelihood of the applicant absconding or tampering with the prosecution witnesses.
In view of the foregoing, it is most prayed that the applicant may be granted the benefit of bail.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:31413 3 MCRC-55562-2025 bail application and prayed for its rejection.

6. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
7.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegations coupled with the fact that the trial is not likely to conclude in near future and prolonged pre-trial detention being an anathema to the concept of liberty, this Court is inclined to extend the benefit of bail to the applicant.
8.
Accordingly, without commenting on merits of the case, this bail application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before it on the dates given by the concerned Court.
